question: Considering only these hand operations (right hand, 8.30–13.33 s), is there an abnormal operation? Select all applicable anomaly types.

options.name: Correct
options.definition: The specified hand operation is explicitly normal throughout the stated scope, with no anomaly or recovery conflict. This does not certify assembly completion.

options.name: Temporal
options.definition: An error concerning when an operation is executed or its temporal organization. The label alone does not identify an exact timing deviation.

options.name: Spatial
options.definition: An error concerning position, orientation or spatial configuration. The label alone does not identify the particular geometry.

options.name: Handling
options.definition: An error in grasping, holding, moving or manipulating an object. This does not itself mean a wrong part or tool was selected.

options.name: Wrong part
options.definition: An unsuitable part is selected or used for the operation. The intended replacement requires separate evidence.

options.name: Wrong tool
options.definition: An unsuitable tool is selected or used for the operation. The correct replacement requires separate evidence.

options.name: Procedural
options.definition: An error concerning procedure requirements. A specific omitted, extra or misordered step requires separate evidence.

observation.description: The right hand holds a silver cylindrical component, rotating and adjusting it with the left hand. The right hand then reaches down to touch the dark mat before returning to the component.

labels.reason: The right hand holds the silver component, but no timing failure, delay, or incorrect temporal organization is visible. The action appears continuous and appropriate for the interval.
